messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: Dedicated pool 'reserved-eu-01' nearing capacity — queue growth observed, user-facing throttles for enterprise tenant 'AcmeCorp'. Alerts: 95% GPU utilization, autoscaler error: rate limit 429 on allocation API. Please respond.

sarah: I'm on it. seeing steady queue growth on the metrics dashboard. customers hitting 429s intermittently. starting timeline collection.

aj: tagging in. can someone grab the autoscaler logs and the allocator stack? I want to see if this is spiking allocations or a throttled API.

infra-bot: Recent autoscaler events (last 15m):
```
2028-10-12T14:02:11Z ERROR allocator: allocation failed status=429 body="rate limit exceeded"
2028-10-12T14:05:02Z WARN  autoscaler: backoff 60s for pool reserved-eu-01
2028-10-12T14:08:47Z INFO  tenant-scheduler: tenant=acmecorp queued_jobs=412 inflight=8
```

jun: looks like the external cloud allocation API returned 429s, autoscaler entered backoff and didn't scale. that explains queue growth.

mike: any evidence of noisy neighbor? reserved-eu-01 should be isolated but noisy jobs can still starve host-level resources (GPU mem or NVMe) and trigger placement failures.

sarah: checking per-tenant usage — acmecorp has a bursty job that spiked to 85% of the pool earlier. other reserved tenants appear idle.

aj: plan: 1) stop autoscaler backoff (force one allocation attempt) 2) create emergency spillover to fallback pool (dedicated-burst) for AcmeCorp while we investigate 3) if noisy tenant confirmed, throttle that tenant's concurrency and evict long-running jobs. low-risk actions first: increase allocation retry and open a temporary ticket with cloud to raise allocation QPS.

jun: I'm running the force allocation now: `infractl autoscaler retry --pool reserved-eu-01 --force`

infra-bot: Command accepted. Allocation retry issued.

sarah: allocation still failing, 429 persists. open support ticket already: CLOUD-67890, requesting ephemeral QPS raise. ETA from cloud is ~30-45m. we need immediate mitigation.

mike: start throttle for the noisy tenant: reduce concurrent_sessions for tenant acme-noisy-process to 2.

aj: execute: `rctl tenant update --tenant-id acme-noisy-process --concurrency 2 --reason "emergency noisy-tenant throttle"`

jun: ran the command, response: OK. started eviction sweep for long-running jobs older than 2h on that tenant.

sarah: seeing a drop in queue growth now (20% reduction). but still under pressure, tail latency high. we should enable spillover for critical SLA customers only. acmecorp is enterprise — enable.

aj: enabling spillover for tenant acmecorp to pool dedicated-burst with 10% capacity. `infractl routing update --tenant acmecorp --spillover-pool dedicated-burst --weight 0.1`

infra-bot: Routing update accepted. Drift: some requests will now be routed to dedicated-burst.

mike: pinging account team to notify Acme support: "we've throttled a noisy job and temporarily routed some traffic to a burst pool to reduce errors. investigating root cause."

sarah: on-call handoff incoming in 10m — I need to step out for a meeting. @mike you're next. I'll record current actions in the incident doc (internal). Key items: autoscaler 429 causing backoff, noisy tenant throttle applied, spillover enabled, cloud ticket CLOUD-67890.

mike: taking over. ack. continuing monitoring. can someone post latest Prometheus query for queue length?

jun: `sum(rate(dedicated_queue_length[1m])) by (pool)` shows reserved-eu-01 dropping from 520 -> 160 over last 12m.

mike: good. continue to watch errors. if 429s stop we can gradually remove throttle but keep spillover. also let's patch autoscaler to not fully backoff on 429s from allocation API — instead exponential backoff capped at 2m. putting a PR in.

aj: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3821 - modifies allocator backoff on rate-limited responses. queued for review.

mike: for customer impact: AcmeCorp saw ~14% of requests 429 between 14:00-14:20, median latency doubled for those windows. notify CS and SOC.

sarah: adding postmortem checklist: 1) root cause - cloud allocation API rate-limiting due to regional surge, 2) mitigation - throttle noisy tenant + spillover + manual allocation retry + cloud QPS request, 3) followups - make autoscaler more resilient to 429, add telemetry to detect noisy tenants faster, update runbook.

oncall-bot: Incident acknowledged by mike. Next action: create incident channel and assign severity.

mike: created #incident/reserved-eu-01-1855007777, severity=P2, notifying accounts and infra managers. I'll stay on until cloud QPS is restored and queue < 50.

aj: thanks team. small ops note — let's avoid evicting more than 10% of tenant jobs in one sweep next time; prefer throttles + controlled eviction.

sarah: noted. handing off final logs and screenshots to incident doc. I'll join the postmortem. back in ~1.5h. :thumbsup:

mike: copy. monitoring channel. will update every 15m or on change.
